author: Contributor 91
about: Volter products use their actual OIDC requests, GitHub and Google social callbacks, linked GitHub funder claims, organization management and device flows; RH2's native Apple sign-in receives the missing-provider token-verification refusal.

steps.name: Monday 5 January, 09:00: Volter registers its products with its identity service
Volter's operator has a Volter identity
Kenji's GitHub account, made on GitHub's sign-up page
Volter's OAuth app registered on GitHub's settings page
The identity operator configures the GitHub app credentials (worker/src/auth.ts)
Volter's OAuth app registered in Google's console
The identity operator configures the Google app credentials (worker/src/auth.ts)
Priya's Google account, made outside the identity API
The identity operator accepts RH2's iOS app audience (APPLE_APP_IDS)
Open Autonomy's GitHub platform token, issued in its operator's account settings
first_github: the identity page opens GitHub sign-in (worker/ui/identity.ts:126)
GitHub asks Kenji to sign in
Kenji gives GitHub his username and password
first_github: Kenji reads the GitHub permissions
Kenji declines until he has checked why sign-in asks for email access
The identity callback passes GitHub's cancellation to its error page
Kenji reads that sign-in was denied; he checks the scopes before trying again
retry_github: the identity page opens GitHub sign-in (worker/ui/identity.ts:126)
retry_github: Kenji reads the GitHub permissions
retry_github: Kenji authorizes the identity app
retry_github: the identity callback trades the code at the GitHub twin and keeps the linked account
The World holds the service's admin token, the operator's setting
The operator signs in at id.volter.ai
The operator registers Twin's console: confidential, the code, refresh and client_credentials grants, the organizations scope
and links it to the organizations door
Open Autonomy's giving page, as its World registers it: native, client_secret_post, no consent page
RH2's pilot, a first-party confidential client whose console and desktop widget sign people in
Substrate's gateway, for a share's pages and visitors
The gateway's origin is a resource its tokens may name
and the gateway is linked to it
The shared client every Volter tool on a machine signs in with, under the id @volter/identity publishes
Orbit Apps' Teams server is a resource
and the shared client is linked to it
Tuesday 6 January, 10:00: Priya signs in to the platform
The platform reads the discovery document
It sends her to authorize with PKCE; with no session, to the sign-in page
The sign-in page offers her identity
platform_google: Priya chooses Google on the identity sign-in page (worker/ui/identity.ts:126)
platform_google: Google shows Priya the account chooser
platform_google: Priya selects her Google account
platform_google: the identity callback exchanges the code and verifies Google keys through its twin
Authorize, signed in, sends her back to the platform with a code
The platform exchanges the code, client_secret_post with its verifier
Userinfo names the Google-signed-in person as Twin reads it (apps/platform/src/identity.ts:239)
The platform reads the same signed-in person through the World alias http://127.0.0.1:8765
The platform reads the same signed-in person through the World alias http://localhost:8765
The platform's own token for the organizations API (client_credentials, client_secret_post)
It finds Priya by her email
She creates Orbit Apps; she is its owner
Twin finds Kenji by email before adding his identity (apps/platform/src/directory.ts:70)
She adds Kenji as a member
and makes him an admin
Kenji opens the organization dashboard to see the team he joined
Twin reads its organization using the same signed resource token through http://127.0.0.1:8765
Twin reads its organization using the same signed resource token through http://localhost:8765
The members: Priya the owner, Kenji an admin
She invites Lena, who has no Volter identity yet, for a week
The pending invitations
Thursday 8 January, 10:00: Lena has accepted a role elsewhere; Priya updates the team
The platform renews its expired organizations token before updating the team
Lena joins another team; Priya cancels the invitation
No invitation is pending
She renames the organization
Away all next week, Priya makes Kenji a second owner
Kenji's organizations, with his role
Kenji by his id
Friday 9 January, 09:30: Kenji signs supercode in on his laptop
@volter/identity opens his browser to authorize, its callback on a port the system picked
harness_github: the identity page opens GitHub sign-in (worker/ui/identity.ts:126)
harness_github: Kenji reads the GitHub permissions
harness_github: the identity callback trades the code at the GitHub twin and keeps the linked account
and the browser returns to the loopback callback with a code
The shared client exchanges it with no secret, its verifier the proof
No ID token names his email, so @volter/identity asks userinfo who signed in
The Teams server verifies Kenji's token against the issuer's keys
Friday 9 January, 11:00: the hour is up; supercode refreshes
tokenFor refreshes for Orbit Apps' Teams server, the audience it verifies
Saturday 10 January, 15:00: supercode on a build machine with no browser
It asks for a device code
and polls: not yet approved
Kenji opens the link, which carries the code
and approves it
Wait the documented five-second device polling interval
The next poll answers the tokens
The laptop replays its rotated predecessor; the zero-grace issuer invalidates this shared-client family
The laptop successor is refused after family invalidation
The other device grant of the same person and shared client is refused too
Kenji starts an ordinary new device sign-in after the family refusal
Kenji approves only the new device code through the normal device page
The new device sign-in issues a fresh grant after invalidation
The newly signed-in device can refresh for its linked Teams resource
Monday 12 January, 16:00: Priya opens a share of Kenji's work
A share's page sends her through the gateway to authorize; her session still holds, so she is back at once
The gateway trades the page's code with its secret, for tokens whose audience is the gateway
and verifies them against the issuer's keys
An hour passes while Priya uses the shared page
An hour on, the page's refresh token is traded the same way
A shared app's visitor link sends her to authorize as a visitor; she is signed in, so she is back at once
The gateway trades the visit's code
and reads her email and name from userinfo, which the ID token keeps out
Tuesday 13 January, 11:00: Kenji gives to a project on Open Autonomy
The giving page reads the discovery document
It sends him to authorize with PKCE; he is signed in, so he is back with a code
The page trades the code with its secret
and verifies the ID token, whose linked GitHub account names the funder, against the issuer's keys
Open Autonomy reads the linked GitHub id's current login (apps/platform/src/give-auth.ts:103)
Wednesday 14 January, 09:00: Priya signs in to Runhuman's console
RH2 reads the discovery document, the device grant's endpoint among it
Signing in as someone else, RH2 asks again with prompt=login: her session does not answer, the sign-in page does
rh_google: Priya continues with Google on the identity screen
rh_google: Google shows Priya the account chooser
rh_google: Priya selects her Google account
rh_google: the identity callback exchanges the code and verifies Google keys through its twin
Authorize sends her back to RH2 with a code
RH2 trades the code with its secret
verifies the ID token (its nonce, audience and expiry) against the keys
and reads her verified address from userinfo
Wednesday 14 January, 14:00: the desktop widget signs her in on her phone
The widget's RH2 asks for a device code, authenticated with its secret
and polls with its secret: not yet approved
RH2's iOS Apple sign-in is refused when the World cannot fetch Apple's keys (apps/rh2-mobile/apple.ts:41,46; Better Auth sign-in.ts:293)
The iOS app falls back to the Google session Priya started earlier today: it opens the widget's code, claiming it for her
and she approves it in the app
The widget waits its five-second interval
and its next poll answers the tokens
Monday 2 February, 10:00: Kenji leaves Orbit Apps
The platform renews its expired organizations token before removing Kenji
First the platform returns him to a plain member, taking back the owner's rights he held
The platform removes him from the organization
He belongs to no organization of the platform
Priya opens a separate organization for a proposed spring client pilot, keeping its access apart from Orbit Apps
Monday 2 March, 10:00: the client declines the spring pilot; Priya keeps Orbit Apps and retires the separate pilot
The platform obtains a current organizations token to retire the separate pilot
Priya deletes the pilot organization she owns, keeping Orbit Apps for the team
The local identity operator configures the permanent ISSUER before Open Autonomy registers its client
Open Autonomy rehearses with its local identity installation and checks the configured issuer
Discovery retains the configured issuer when reached through http://localhost:8765
Discovery retains the configured issuer when reached through https://id.volter.ai
